segments.t: Back in the kitchen, Max and the cooks try to guess what kind of movies their stern boss German watches at home, and his eerie answer plunges the restaurant into a zombie horror story.
Понятно, какое кино вы дома смотрите.
Мультики дают ошибочное представление о людях.
Let's go through each line as German describes his love of zombie films.
Понятно, какое кино вы дома смотрите.
'It is clear what kind of movies you watch at home.' The adverb 'at home' is distinct from 'homeward' and sits right before the verb.
'No, that is completely untrue.' Joining 'not' directly to 'truth' creates the single noun 'untruth' or 'lie'.
'Then what, sweet cartoons?' Max guesses the most innocent genre he can think of.
Мультики дают ошибочное представление о людях.
'Cartoons give a mistaken impression of people.' The noun for 'notion' or 'impression' takes the preposition 'about' plus the prepositional case.
'Movies about zombies are another matter.' Like 'kino', the borrowed noun 'zombie' never changes its form for number or case.
'In those, everything is honest and real.' The adverb built with 'po-' and '-omu' means 'fairly' or 'honestly'.
'People are ready to eat each other up.' The plural short-form adjective 'ready' agrees with the plural subject 'people'.
'Lyova, your glove fell.' Instead of 'your glove', Russian says 'by you the glove fell'.
'And your arm fell off too!' In Russian, one single feminine word covers both 'hand' and 'arm'.
'Oh, pick it up, please.' Even as a zombie, polite Lyova says 'please' when asking Max to pick up his arm.
'Quiet, do not scare me like that!' The adverb 'quietly' is used on its own as an urgent command meaning 'quiet!' or 'hush!'.
'What kind of jokes are these, Lyova?' Max backs away in horror as the zombie nightmare begins. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Понятно, какое кино вы дома смотрите.
Мультики дают ошибочное представление о людях.
Remember that Russian uses the exact same feminine noun for both 'hand' and 'arm', just as one word covers both 'foot' and 'leg'. See you in the next scene.
